title: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces in 6G Radio Localization: A Survey of Recent Developments, Opportunities, and Challenges
affiliation: Tallinn University of Technology / Chalmers University of Technology
domain: RIS / 6G / Radio Localization / mmWave / THz / Near-Field / ISAC / SLAM

analysis_policy.focus: Extract research questions framework, multi-part scenario tables, taxonomy diagrams, frequency band categorization, near/far-field distinction
analysis_policy.depth: Full paper analysis covering fundamentals, state-of-art by frequency/scenario, and future directions

section_flow.title: Introduction
section_flow.summary: Establishes 6G localization challenges, positions RIS as alternative to multiple BSs. Introduces 3 research questions. Compares with existing surveys (Table I-II). Describes systematic review method with search string.

section_flow.title: RIS in Radio Localization
subsections: C. RIS Support for Radio Localization
section_flow.summary: RIS types (reflective, transmissive, hybrid, STAR, active), signal/channel models, localization fundamentals. Taxonomy with measurements, algorithms, RIS types, deployment considerations, performance metrics.

section_flow.title: State of the Art in RIS-Assisted Radio Localization
subsections: A. RIS-Assisted Outdoor and Far-Field Localization
section_flow.summary: Core literature survey organized by scenario (outdoor/indoor) and propagation model (far-field/near-field). Sub-organized by frequency bands (CRF <24GHz, High Freq >24GHz). Tables IV-IX summarize 150+ references.

section_flow.title: Challenges and Research Outlook
section_flow.summary: 13 research challenges: Availability/Scalability/Privacy, Mobile User, Multi-User, Multi-Frequency, ISAC Integration, Deployment, AI Control, Low Latency, RIS Standardization, Multi-Operator, Mobility Control, Hardware Limitations, Calibration, New Antenna Technologies, From RIS to SIM.

section_flow.title: Conclusion
section_flow.summary: Synthesizes survey contributions on RIS-assisted localization taxonomy, recent advancements, opportunities, and challenges.

rhetorical_contract.promise: Comprehensive overview of RIS technology for radio localization in 6G networks with taxonomy, recent developments, and future directions
rhetorical_contract.delivery_mechanism: 3 Research Questions → RIS Fundamentals → State-of-Art by Scenario/Frequency → Challenges/Future Directions
rhetorical_contract.unique_contribution: First comprehensive RIS localization survey with systematic review methodology, detailed taxonomy, multi-table state-of-art breakdown by scenario/frequency/propagation model

research_questions_framework: Q1: How has RIS been used for localization in 6G networks?
Q2: What are the current trends and developments in RIS for 6G localization?
Q3: What are future directions, challenges, and limitations?
key_gap_findings: Most studies focus on accuracy, less on coverage/availability
Hardware limitations and pixel failures problematic

methodology.survey_approach: Systematic literature review with explicit search string, inclusion/exclusion criteria, reproducibility emphasis
methodology.search_string: (RIS OR IRS OR LIS) AND (localization OR positioning) AND (6G)

style.register: Technical survey with systematic review rigor
rhetorical_patterns: Tables compare surveys by topic dimensions
State-of-art uses thematic groupings (a, b, c, d, e, f, g)
characteristic_phrases: In this survey, we seek answers to the following questions
The unique aspects of our work are stated below
Based on the review performed in the previous section
It is, thus, an important area to explore

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Open the survey with 3 explicit research questions that drive the paper's organization and are answered in dedicated sections
structure: Introduction states 3 numbered research questions (Q1, Q2, Q3)
Each major section explicitly answers one question
Opening paragraph maps sections to questions: 'Section II answers Q1, Section III answers Q2, Section IV answers Q3'
Comparison table shows how existing surveys address these questions
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Q1 → Section II (RIS fundamentals), Q2 → Section III (State-of-Art), Q3 → Section IV (Challenges)
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Clear purpose statement; enables reader to self-select sections; demonstrates unique scope vs existing work
reusable_writing_recipes.complexity: Low - straightforward to implement but highly effective

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Include a dedicated subsection declaring the systematic review methodology with search string, databases, and inclusion/exclusion criteria
structure: Subsection titled 'Review Method' or 'Search Strategy'
State keywords derived from research questions
Present complete search string with logical operators
List databases searched (IEEE Xplore, etc.)
Describe inclusion/exclusion criteria
Mention backward referencing for completeness
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section I-B provides search string: ('RIS' OR 'IRS' OR 'LIS') AND ('localization' OR 'positioning') AND ('6G')
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Establishes academic rigor; ensures reproducibility; differentiates from informal reviews

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Organize state-of-art literature into multiple tables based on scenario (indoor/outdoor), propagation model (near/far-field), and frequency band
structure: Create separate tables for major scenario combinations
Consistent columns: RIS Type, Ref, Frequency, Link, System, Purpose, Technique, Performance Metric
Group references within tables by thematic focus (a. Foundational, b. Novel techniques, c. ISAC, etc.)
Use abbreviation legend in table caption (R=Reflective, A=Active, S=STAR, H=Hybrid)
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Tables IV (CRF Outdoor), V-VII (High Freq Outdoor - 3 parts), VIII (Indoor), IX (Near-Field)
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Enables focused lookup; reveals research distribution across scenarios; comprehensive coverage demonstration

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Within each major subsection, organize references into labeled thematic groups using alphabetical markers
structure: Use italicized headers with letters: 'a) Foundational studies:', 'b) Novel techniques:', 'c) ISAC:', etc.
Each group contains 2-5 paragraph summaries of related works
Maintain consistent grouping categories across similar sections when possible
Reference specific table entries for each work discussed
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section III.A.2 uses: a) Foundational, b) Advanced techniques, c) Beamforming, d) Multiuser, e) Special scenarios, f) High frequency sensing, g) Practical applications
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Enables thematic reading; reveals research trends within domains; assists navigation

reusable_writing_recipes.description: Present the paper's taxonomy using both diagrammatic (tree structure) and illustrated (scenario visualization) figures
structure: Figure A: Tree-structured taxonomy diagram with hierarchical categories
Figure B: Illustrated taxonomy showing scenarios in visual form
Both figures use same categorical structure
Caption explains the taxonomy dimensions
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Fig. 6 (taxonomy tree) + Fig. 7 (illustrated scenarios) both show RIS localization dimensions
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Appeals to different learning styles; reinforces understanding; enables quick reference

reusable_writing_recipes.recipe_name: Bullet-Point Research Directions with Explanatory Paragraphs
reusable_writing_recipes.description: Present future research directions as bullet points with detailed explanatory paragraphs for each
structure: Use bullet point format with italicized topic header
Follow header with 1-2 detailed paragraphs explaining the challenge
Include specific sub-challenges within each direction
Reference related works that motivate the direction
Suggest specific research questions or approaches
reusable_writing_recipes.example_application: Section IV presents 13 research directions (Availability, Mobile User, Multi-User, Multi-Frequency, ISAC, Deployment, AI, Low Latency, Standardization, Multi-Operator, Mobility Control, Hardware, Calibration, New Antenna, SIM)
reusable_writing_recipes.rhetorical_effect: Comprehensive future roadmap; inspires follow-on research; demonstrates author expertise beyond surveying

key_concepts.ris_localization_advantage: RIS enables localization with single BS (vs 4+ traditional BSs), provides infrastructure reduction, energy efficiency
key_concepts.near_vs_far_field: Near-field uses spherical wave model with wavefront curvature; Far-field uses plane wave assumption; Near-field region increases with frequency and RIS size
key_concepts.frequency_progression: CRF (<24GHz) for longer range, mmW/THz (>24GHz) for higher accuracy but limited coverage
key_concepts.key_metrics: CRLB and PEB are most common bounds for theoretical localization accuracy analysis
